record.body: Any sound can be described as a sum of pure tones at different frequencies, and the Fourier transform is the mathematical operation that finds how much energy a recording contains at each frequency. Bioacousticians divide the spectrum into bands, for example low frequencies below 1 kilohertz where many large mammals call, mid frequencies where most birds sing, and high frequencies above 20 kilohertz where bats echolocate, and they measure how much energy falls in each band. Band occupancy, the share of total energy in each band, is a simple summary that already reveals whether a recording is dominated by bird song, by insect chorus, or by low engine rumble. All three soundscape layers occupy bands, so band analysis is one tool for separating biophony from geophony and anthrophony.

demo.code:
TITLE = 'Frequency Bands and the Fourier Transform'
BANDS = {'low <1 kHz': 30, 'mid 1-8 kHz': 50, 'high >8 kHz': 20}
tot = float(sum(BANDS.values()))
print('Record: ' + TITLE)
print('Total: %d' % int(tot))
for k in sorted(BANDS):
    print('%s: %d (%.1f percent)' % (k, BANDS[k], 100.0 * BANDS[k] / tot))
demo.expected_output:
Record: Frequency Bands and the Fourier Transform
Total: 100
high >8 kHz: 20 (20.0 percent)
low <1 kHz: 30 (30.0 percent)
mid 1-8 kHz: 50 (50.0 percent)
